sourceNote: Clause numbers and titles follow EN 301 549 V4.1.1 (2026-09), published by ETSI, CEN and CENELEC on 2 September 2026 under the European Commission's standardisation request M/587 for the European Accessibility Act. Rows were extracted from the official PDF by scripts/en301549/build-v4-checklist.mjs, reconciled against Annex C and the clause A.2 conformance tables, and diffed against the V3.2.1 dataset. Plain-language summaries are original accessibility.build prose, verified against the published standard on 19 October 2026. WCAG-mapped clause summaries reuse this site's criterion descriptions.

chapters.13: ICT providing relay or emergency service access

A.1.label: Where the ICT is, or includes, a web page

A.2.label: Where the ICT is, or includes, a non-web document

A.3.label: Where the ICT is, or includes, non-web software that provides a user interface

A.4.label: Where the ICT is, or includes, hardware

rows.title: Usage without vision
rows.summary: Where ICT has visual modes of operation, it must provide at least one mode of operation that does not require vision. Annex C treats each criterion in clause 4.2 as met when the Annex B requirements mapped to it are met, or when there is evidence of the outcome.
rows.changeNote: Written with "shall" in V4.1.1: the functional performance criteria are now testable requirements (Annex C.4.2) rather than descriptive statements.

rows.title: Usage with limited vision
rows.summary: Where ICT has visual modes of operation, it must provide features, such as magnification, a reduced field of vision, or control of contrast, brightness and intensity, that let people with limited vision use it.
rows.changeNote: Written with "shall" in V4.1.1: the functional performance criteria are now testable requirements (Annex C.4.2) rather than descriptive statements.

rows.title: Usage without perception of colour
rows.summary: Where ICT has visual modes of operation, it must provide a visual mode that does not depend on the user perceiving colour.
rows.changeNote: Written with "shall" in V4.1.1: the functional performance criteria are now testable requirements (Annex C.4.2) rather than descriptive statements.

rows.title: Usage without hearing
rows.summary: Where ICT has auditory modes of operation, it must provide at least one mode of operation that does not require hearing.
rows.changeNote: Written with "shall" in V4.1.1: the functional performance criteria are now testable requirements (Annex C.4.2) rather than descriptive statements.

rows.title: Usage with limited hearing
rows.summary: Where ICT has auditory modes of operation, it must provide enhanced audio features, such as clarity enhancement, background-noise reduction, a wider volume range, or a way to connect assistive listening devices.
rows.changeNote: Written with "shall" in V4.1.1: the functional performance criteria are now testable requirements (Annex C.4.2) rather than descriptive statements.

rows.title: Usage with no or limited vocal capability
rows.summary: Where ICT requires vocal input, it must provide at least one mode of operation that does not require the user to produce speech or other vocal sounds.

previous.title: Usage with no or limited vocal capability

rows.changeNote: Written with "shall" in V4.1.1: the functional performance criteria are now testable requirements (Annex C.4.2) rather than descriptive statements.

rows.title: Usage with limited manipulation or strength
rows.summary: Where ICT requires manual actions, it must provide features that let users operate it through alternative actions that do not need fine manipulation, simultaneous actions, or hand strength.

previous.title: Usage with limited manipulation or strength

rows.changeNote: Written with "shall" in V4.1.1: the functional performance criteria are now testable requirements (Annex C.4.2) rather than descriptive statements.

rows.title: Usage with limited reach
rows.summary: Where ICT is stationary, free-standing, or installed, every element needed to operate it must be within reach of all users, including wheelchair users and people of different statures.
rows.changeNote: Written with "shall" in V4.1.1 and now scoped to stationary, free-standing or installed ICT.

rows.title: Minimize photosensitive seizure triggers
rows.summary: Where ICT has visual modes of operation, its default mode must minimise the potential for triggering photosensitive seizures, or, for audiovisual material, warn in advance that triggers may be present.
rows.changeNote: Written with "shall" in V4.1.1; the seizure-safe mode must now be the default mode, or audiovisual material must carry an advance warning.

rows.title: Usage with limited cognition, language or learning
rows.summary: Where ICT provides information or requires interaction, it must provide features or presentation that make it simpler and easier to understand, operate, and use, such as adjustable timings, error suggestions, a logical focus order, audio output of text, and tasks broken into easy steps.

previous.title: Usage with limited cognition, language or learning

rows.changeNote: Written with "shall" in V4.1.1 and now scoped to ICT that provides information or requires user interaction.

rows.title: Privacy
rows.summary: Where ICT provides accessibility features, using them must not reduce the user's privacy: for example private listening through a personal headset, no spoken version of masked characters, and user control over legal, financial, and personal data.
rows.changeNote: Written with "shall" in V4.1.1: privacy must be maintained whenever accessibility features are used.

rows.title: Closed functionality
rows.summary: ICT with closed functionality must meet the applicable requirements of clauses 5.2 to 13 for those closed functions.

rows.title: Assistive technology and closed functionality
rows.summary: Closed functionality must be usable without the user attaching, connecting, or installing assistive technology, and must meet clauses 5.1.3 to 5.1.6 as applicable. Personal headsets and personal induction loops do not count as assistive technology here.
rows.changeNote: Titled "Assistive technology" in V3.2.1.

rows.title: Auditory output of visual information
rows.summary: Where visual information is needed to use closed functionality, the ICT must provide at least one non-visual way to use it that includes auditory output.
rows.changeNote: Titled "Audio output of visual information" in V3.2.1.

rows.title: Auditory output delivery including speech
rows.summary: Auditory output used as non-visual access must be delivered either by a mechanism included with the ICT or through a standard personal headset connection that can be used without vision.

rows.title: Auditory output correlation
rows.summary: Where closed functionality provides auditory output and information is displayed on screen, the auditory output must let the user correlate what they hear with what is on the display.
rows.changeNote: Advisory ("should") in V3.2.1; a testable requirement ("shall") in V4.1.1.

rows.title: Speech output user control
rows.summary: Speech output must be interruptible and repeatable on request, where security requirements permit.

rows.title: Speech output automatic interruption
rows.summary: The ICT must interrupt current speech output when a user action occurs and when new speech output begins.

rows.title: Auditory output for non-text content
rows.summary: Where closed functionality presents non-text content other than video, any alternative for it must be delivered as auditory output including speech, unless the content is pure decoration or visual formatting only.
rows.changeNote: Titled "Speech output for non-text content" in V3.2.1.

rows.title: Auditory output for video information
rows.summary: Where pre-recorded video is needed to use closed functionality, the ICT must provide an auditory equivalent for that video, and must pass on any auditory equivalent supplied with video from another source.
rows.changeNote: Titled "Speech output for video information" in V3.2.1.

rows.title: Masked entry
rows.summary: Speech output must not read masked characters (such as PIN digits) aloud unless the user explicitly chooses audible unmasked entry.

rows.title: Private access to personal data
rows.summary: Auditory output containing private data must only be delivered through a private listening mechanism (such as a headset) or another user-chosen private means.

rows.title: Non-interfering audio output
rows.summary: The ICT must not automatically play interfering audio lasting longer than three seconds at the same time as the speech output.

rows.title: Private listening volume
rows.summary: Where auditory output is delivered through a private listening mechanism, at least one non-visual way to control the volume must exist.

rows.title: Speaker volume
rows.summary: Where auditory output is delivered through speakers, a non-visual incremental volume control with amplification up to at least 65 dBA must be provided.

rows.title: Volume reset
rows.summary: On shared-use ICT, a function must reset the volume to 65 dBA or less after every use.

rows.title: Spoken languages
rows.summary: Speech output must be in the same human language as the displayed content, with narrow exceptions such as proper names, technical terms, and languages the ICT cannot speak.

rows.title: Non-visual error identification
rows.summary: Where an input error is automatically detected, speech output must identify and describe the item in error.

rows.title: Receipts, tickets, and transactional outputs
rows.summary: Receipts, tickets, and other transaction outputs from self-service ICT must have their essential information available via speech output (printed copies themselves are exempt).

rows.title: Functionality closed to text enlargement
rows.summary: Where functionality is closed to text-enlargement features, the ICT must itself provide a mode where text needed for all functionality is legible at distance-appropriate sizes.

rows.title: Visual output for auditory information
rows.summary: Where auditory information is needed to use closed functions, the ICT must provide equivalent visual information, such as captions.

rows.title: Functionality closed to keyboards
rows.summary: Where closed functionality cannot be operated with a keyboard or keyboard interface, it must still be operable without vision as clause 5.1.3 requires.
rows.changeNote: Titled "Closed functionality" in V3.2.1.

rows.title: Input focus
rows.summary: Where input focus can be moved to an element, it must also be movable away from that element using the same mechanism, so focus cannot get trapped.

rows.title: Access without speech
rows.summary: Where speech is needed to operate closed functions, at least one alternative input mechanism that does not require speech must be provided.

rows.title: Identify input purpose (closed functionality)
rows.summary: Where closed functionality has input fields that collect information about the user and serve one of the purposes listed in WCAG 2.2 (name, address, email and so on), at least one mode of operation must present the purpose of each field in audio.

rows.title: Activation of accessibility features
rows.summary: Documented accessibility features must be activatable without relying on a method that the feature's target users cannot use.

rows.title: Biometrics
rows.summary: ICT using biometrics must not make one particular biological characteristic the only way to identify a user or control the ICT.

rows.title: Preservation of accessibility information during conversion
rows.summary: When ICT converts information, it must preserve all documented non-proprietary accessibility information the destination format can hold.

previous.title: Preservation of accessibility information during conversion

rows.title: Tactilely discernible operable parts
rows.summary: ICT that needs manual operation must offer a mode in which every manually operated function can be controlled without vision, using only parts that can be found and told apart by touch (a screen edge, corner, or tactile marker counts).
rows.changeNote: Was 5.5.2 (Operable parts discernibility) in V3.2.1.

rows.title: Tactile or auditory status
rows.summary: Where a locking or toggle control shows its status visually, at least one mode must expose the status by touch or sound as well.

rows.title: Visual status
rows.summary: Where a locking or toggle control exposes its status non-visually, at least one mode must make the status visually determinable too.

rows.title: Key repeat
rows.summary: A key-repeat function that cannot be turned off must allow a repeat delay of at least 2 seconds and a rate adjustable down to 1 character per 2 seconds.

rows.title: Double-strike key acceptance
rows.summary: On keyboards and keypads, the delay for rejecting an accidental identical second keystroke must be adjustable up to at least 0.5 seconds.

rows.title: Simultaneous user actions
rows.summary: Any operation requiring simultaneous user actions must have at least one mode of operation that does not.

rows.title: Content technology
rows.summary: Authoring tools must meet clauses 5.10.2 to 5.10.5 to the extent that the output format supports the relevant accessibility information.
rows.changeNote: Was 11.8.1 (Content technology) in V3.2.1.

rows.title: Accessible content creation
rows.summary: Authoring tools must enable and guide the production of content that conforms to clause 9 (web), clause 10 (non-web documents), or clause 11 (non-web software), as applicable.
rows.changeNote: Was 11.8.2 (Accessible content creation) in V3.2.1.

rows.title: Preservation of accessibility information in transformations
rows.summary: Restructuring and re-coding transformations must preserve accessibility information where the output technology can hold it.

previous.title: Preservation of accessibility information in transformations

rows.changeNote: Was 11.8.3 (Preservation of accessibility information in transformations) in V3.2.1.

rows.title: Repair assistance
rows.summary: Where an authoring tool can detect that content fails a requirement of clause 9, 10, or 11, it must offer repair suggestions.
rows.changeNote: Was 11.8.4 (Repair assistance) in V3.2.1.

rows.title: Templates
rows.summary: Where templates are offered, at least one accessible template supporting conformant content must be available and identified as such.
rows.changeNote: Was 11.8.5 (Templates) in V3.2.1.

rows.title: Communication client
rows.summary: A communication client that supports real-time voice with or within a communication system must meet every applicable requirement of clauses 6.1 and 6.3 to 6.6 when communicating, and, if it is part of a terminal that handles text, every applicable clause 6.2 (RTT) requirement too.

rows.title: Communication system
rows.summary: A communication system that provides real-time voice to its own clients must meet every applicable requirement of clauses 6.1 to 6.6 when communicating with them. Component parts such as routers can be tested by including them in a system under test.

rows.title: System connecting to another communication system
rows.summary: A communication system that connects to other real-time voice systems must meet every applicable requirement of clauses 6.1 to 6.6 when communicating with those other systems.

rows.title: System with roaming visiting client
rows.summary: A communication system that accepts a visiting (roaming) client from another compatible system must meet every applicable requirement of clauses 6.1 to 6.6 when communicating with that visiting client.

rows.title: Client in emergency communications
rows.summary: A communication client that provides emergency communications must meet every applicable requirement of clauses 6.1 and 6.3 to 6.6 during an emergency communication, plus all applicable clause 6.2 (RTT) requirements where the terminal handles text.

rows.title: Emergency communications
rows.summary: A communication system that carries real-time voice emergency communications to public safety answering points (PSAPs) must meet every applicable requirement of clauses 6.1 to 6.6 during the emergency communication.

rows.title: System with roaming visiting client in an emergency
rows.summary: A communication system handling an emergency communication from a visiting (roaming) client of another system must meet every applicable requirement of clauses 6.1 to 6.6 when connecting that client to a PSAP.

rows.title: System with client in emergency visiting another country
rows.summary: A communication system whose own client is in another country must meet every applicable requirement of clauses 6.1 to 6.6 when that client contacts a PSAP in the visited country. This covers VoIP-style systems that do not use call-control roaming.

rows.title: Voice communication interoperability
rows.summary: ICT that connects to other ICT for real-time voice must document the specifications it uses so that voice interoperates, covering at least 100 Hz to 7 000 Hz, either by mutual agreement with the other ICT or by implementing ITU-T G.722.

rows.title: Audio bandwidth for capture and presentation for voice communication
rows.summary: ICT with a user interface for real-time voice must be able to capture, communicate, and present speech over a frequency range of at least 250 Hz to 7 000 Hz.
rows.changeNote: Was 6.1 (Audio bandwidth for speech) in V3.2.1.

rows.title: Audio presentation in attached listening devices for voice communication (recommendation)
rows.summary: Advisory: ICT with an interface for external presentation of voice (such as attached listening devices) should be able to present audio from at least 100 Hz up to 7 000 Hz.

rows.title: Synchronization of subtitles (recommendation)
rows.summary: Advisory: where subtitles are provided for real-time voice communication, the delay between a word being spoken and its first character appearing should not exceed 2 seconds.

rows.title: RTT functionality
rows.summary: ICT that provides real-time voice communication must also provide real-time text (RTT) communication, which implicitly covers interoperation for RTT wherever it interoperates for voice, and multi-party RTT where multi-party voice is supported.
rows.changeNote: Titled "RTT communication" in V3.2.1.

rows.title: Concurrent voice and RTT
rows.summary: Where ICT provides real-time voice and supports RTT, it must allow voice and RTT to be used at the same time.
rows.changeNote: Titled "Concurrent voice and text" in V3.2.1.

rows.title: Single user action
rows.summary: ICT with RTT must let a single user action act on all requested or established media (voice, RTT, and any other media) when starting, answering, modifying, holding, transferring, or ending a communication.

rows.title: Distinguishable display
rows.summary: Displayed RTT must show text from different sources, and the text the user sends, with each source indicated and told apart; a simple identifier such as Speaker 1 is enough.
rows.changeNote: Titled "Visually distinguishable display" in V3.2.1.

rows.title: Active communicator indication
rows.summary: Where ICT provides speaker indication for voice, it must indicate every active communicator, including those using RTT, so all parties know who is communicating.
rows.changeNote: Was 6.2.2.3 (Speaker identification) in V3.2.1.

rows.title: Indication of audio with RTT
rows.summary: ICT that supports RTT must display a real-time indicator of non-local audio activity, so a user who cannot hear knows when someone is speaking.

previous.title: Visual indicator of Audio with RTT

rows.changeNote: Was 6.2.2.4 (Visual indicator of Audio with RTT) in V3.2.1.

rows.title: Presentation of relative time order of text
rows.summary: RTT must be presented as blocks of text from each source, including the local user, ordered by the moment each block ends (sentence-ending punctuation plus a space, a line separator, or a 5-second pause); editing a block moves it to the time of the last edit.

previous.title: Visual indicator of Audio with RTT

rows.changeNote: Titled "Visual indicator of Audio with RTT" in V3.2.1.

rows.title: Review of RTT communication contents
rows.summary: Users must be able to review the whole RTT content of a communication while it is in progress and, if the communication is recorded, after it has ended.

rows.title: DTMF touch-tone generation during RTT operations
rows.summary: A communication client that supports touch-tone (DTMF) signalling on voice calls must provide a way to send touch-tones for the characters 0 to 9, star, hash, and A to D that is distinct from typing those characters as RTT and compatible with the standard method for voice calls.
rows.changeNote: Titled "Interoperability" in V3.2.1.

rows.title: RTT responsiveness
rows.summary: RTT input must reach the network or platform within 500 ms of the smallest reliably composed unit of text being available, so text truly flows in real time.

rows.title: Adding and erasing of RTT input
rows.summary: The RTT user interface must let users enter new text and erase text from the current end of what they typed, without being blocked by a new line or other delimiter in earlier text; automatic corrections count as erasure too.

rows.title: Processing rate of RTT
rows.summary: ICT that supports multi-party communication with RTT must be able to receive and process RTT at a total of 90 characters per second from at least 3 simultaneous sources sending 30 characters per second each.

rows.title: Character representation
rows.summary: RTT must handle at least a subset of ISO/IEC 10646 that covers Latin-1, the writing directions and characters of the languages of the intended regions, any emoji the platform supports, the replacement character U+FFFD for lost or unsupported characters, and any characters the presentation protocol uses.

rows.title: RTT input methods
rows.summary: A communication client that supports RTT must accept RTT input through every method the ICT offers for general text input.

rows.title: RTT media establishment and use
rows.summary: Regardless of system or client settings, it must be possible to request a communication with RTT media, to answer a request and have RTT added whether or not it was in the original request, and for any party to upgrade an existing communication to include RTT.

rows.title: RTT interoperability
rows.summary: ICT that connects to other ICT for real-time voice must document how its RTT interoperates with that other ICT, either by mutual agreement or, as the fallback, by implementing ITU-T T.140 with IETF RFC 4103 as updated by RFC 9071.
rows.changeNote: Was 6.2.3 (Interoperability) in V3.2.1.

rows.title: Caller ID
rows.summary: Caller ID and similar functions must be available in text form and be programmatically determinable, unless the functionality is closed.

rows.title: Alternatives to voice-based services
rows.summary: Where real-time voice services offer voicemail, auto-attendant, or interactive voice response, the same information and tasks must be achievable without hearing or speech.

rows.title: Resolution
rows.summary: Real-time video used with voice communication must support at least QVGA resolution, and preferably VGA or better.

rows.title: Frame rate
rows.summary: Real-time video used with voice communication must support at least 20 frames per second, and preferably 30 or more.

rows.title: Synchronization between audio and video
rows.summary: The time difference between speech and video presented to the user must not exceed 100 ms, keeping lip-reading viable.

rows.title: Indicator of audio with video
rows.summary: Where real-time video is part of voice communication, the ICT must provide a real-time indicator of audio activity, so a user who cannot hear knows when someone is talking.

previous.title: Visual indicator of audio with video

rows.changeNote: Titled "Visual indicator of audio with video" in V3.2.1.

rows.title: Indication of all active communication participants
rows.summary: Where ICT provides speaker indication for voice users in video communication, it must indicate every active communicator, including those who are signing.

previous.title: Speaker identification with video (sign language) communication

rows.changeNote: Titled "Speaker identification with video (sign language) communication" in V3.2.1.

rows.title: Alternatives to video-based services (recommendation)
rows.summary: Advisory: where real-time video services offer answering machine, auto-attendant, or interactive response facilities, users should be able to access them through video as well.

rows.title: Total conversation provision
rows.summary: ICT that provides real-time voice and includes real-time video must provide total conversation: RTT meeting clause 6.2, voice meeting clause 6.1, and video meeting clause 6.5, while also meeting clauses 6.3 and 6.4.

rows.title: Total conversation interoperability
rows.summary: ICT that connects to other ICT for voice and video must document the specifications by which its video interoperates with that other ICT, either by mutual agreement or by implementing ITU-T H.264 (at least version 10, constrained baseline level 3) and, where codecs are negotiated, H.265 or VP8 to avoid transcoding.

rows.title: Subtitle playback
rows.summary: ICT that displays video with synchronized audio must have a mode that displays the available subtitles, and where closed subtitles are part of the content, must let the user choose to display them.
rows.changeNote: Titled "Captioning playback" in V3.2.1.

rows.title: Subtitle synchronization
rows.summary: Where ICT displays subtitles, each subtitle must appear within 100 ms of the timecode attached to it.
rows.changeNote: Titled "Captioning synchronization" in V3.2.1.

rows.title: Preservation of subtitles
rows.summary: ICT that transmits, converts, or records video with synchronized audio must preserve subtitle data, including presentational data such as screen position, colours, text style, and fonts, so the subtitles can still be displayed as clause 7.1.1 requires.
rows.changeNote: Titled "Preservation of captioning" in V3.2.1.

rows.title: Subtitle characteristics
rows.summary: Where ICT controls how its subtitles are presented, users must be able to adapt the displayed characteristics of subtitles to their own needs, except where subtitles are displayed as unmodifiable characters.
rows.changeNote: Titled "Captions characteristics" in V3.2.1.

rows.title: Spoken subtitles
rows.summary: ICT that displays video with synchronized audio must have a mode that plays spoken subtitles when they are available; it does not have to generate them from text subtitles.
rows.changeNote: Reworded: the player must be able to output spoken subtitles that are available, not generate them.

rows.title: Audio description playback
rows.summary: A mechanism must exist to select and play available audio description to the default audio channel.

rows.title: Audio description synchronization
rows.summary: Audio description playback must stay synchronized with the audio-visual content.

rows.title: Preservation of audio description
rows.summary: ICT that transmits, converts, or records video must preserve audio description data for downstream playback.

rows.title: User control of audiovisual accessibility features
rows.summary: ICT whose primary purpose is playing video with synchronized audio, and which controls the activation of subtitles, audio description, and spoken subtitles, must let the user switch any of those on or off with a single action at the same level of interaction as the volume control.

previous.title: User controls for captions and audio description

rows.changeNote: Titled "User controls for captions and audio description" in V3.2.1.

rows.title: Speech volume gain
rows.summary: Hardware with speech output that is typically held to the ear must let the user raise the speech volume to at least 18 dB of conversational gain.
rows.changeNote: Titled "Speech volume range" in V3.2.1.

rows.title: Incremental volume control
rows.summary: Where the volume control is incremental, at least one intermediate step of 12 dB gain above the lowest setting must exist.

rows.title: Fixed-line devices and handsets
rows.summary: Fixed-line communication devices and wired handsets held to the ear must provide magnetic coupling to hearing technologies meeting ETSI ES 200 381-1, and must be marked as compatible with magnetic coupling if designed for public use.
rows.changeNote: Titled "Fixed-line devices" in V3.2.1.

rows.title: Wireless communication devices
rows.summary: Wireless communication devices held to the ear must provide magnetic coupling to hearing technologies meeting ETSI ES 200 381-2.

rows.title: Display screen location
rows.summary: Display screens that are part of stationary ICT must be placed so that no part of the display is lower than 800 mm above the floor of the access space.
rows.changeNote: Clause 8.3 (stationary ICT) was rewritten in V4.1.1 with new reach, height and free-space rules; its numbers do not correspond to V3.2.1.

rows.title: Presentation of information necessary for the operation of stationary ICT (no design restrictions)
rows.summary: Where nothing in the design prevents it, all information needed to operate stationary ICT must be placed no higher than 1 600 mm above the floor of the access space (Set 1).
rows.changeNote: Clause 8.3 (stationary ICT) was rewritten in V4.1.1 with new reach, height and free-space rules; its numbers do not correspond to V3.2.1.

rows.title: Presentation of information necessary for the operation of stationary ICT (with design restrictions)
rows.summary: Where functional or design requirements prevent placing it lower, information needed to operate stationary ICT must be placed no higher than 2 000 mm above the floor of the access space (Set 2).
rows.changeNote: Clause 8.3 (stationary ICT) was rewritten in V4.1.1 with new reach, height and free-space rules; its numbers do not correspond to V3.2.1.

rows.title: Control location (vertical, no design restrictions)
rows.summary: Where operable parts can be placed or duplicated freely, at least one of each type must sit between 800 mm and 1 100 mm above the floor (Set 1).
rows.changeNote: Clause 8.3 (stationary ICT) was rewritten in V4.1.1 with new reach, height and free-space rules; its numbers do not correspond to V3.2.1.

rows.title: Control location (vertical, with design restrictions)
rows.summary: Where operable parts cannot be duplicated or placed in the 800 mm to 1 100 mm band, those parts must sit between 380 mm and 1 220 mm above the floor and must not be blocked by obstructions (Set 2).
rows.changeNote: Clause 8.3 (stationary ICT) was rewritten in V4.1.1 with new reach, height and free-space rules; its numbers do not correspond to V3.2.1.

rows.title: Control location (horizontal)
rows.summary: At least one of each type of operable part on stationary ICT must lie within a horizontal span of no more than 900 mm, so users do not have to move to reach all controls.
rows.changeNote: Clause 8.3 (stationary ICT) was rewritten in V4.1.1 with new reach, height and free-space rules; its numbers do not correspond to V3.2.1.

rows.title: Reach depth (no design restrictions)
rows.summary: Where operable parts can be placed or duplicated freely, at least one of each type must be within 300 mm of the edge of the ICT nearest the user (Set 1).
rows.changeNote: Clause 8.3 (stationary ICT) was rewritten in V4.1.1 with new reach, height and free-space rules; its numbers do not correspond to V3.2.1.

rows.title: Reach depth (with design restrictions)
rows.summary: Where operable parts cannot be duplicated or placed within 300 mm, at least one of each type must be within 510 mm (forward reach) or 610 mm (side reach) of the edge of the ICT nearest the user (Set 2).
rows.changeNote: Clause 8.3 (stationary ICT) was rewritten in V4.1.1 with new reach, height and free-space rules; its numbers do not correspond to V3.2.1.

rows.title: Obstructed forward reach (no design constraints)
rows.summary: Where stationary ICT has an integral obstruction in front of the controls and nothing requires it to be deeper than 300 mm, the obstruction must be no higher than 800 mm and no deeper than 300 mm (Set 1).
rows.changeNote: Clause 8.3 (stationary ICT) was rewritten in V4.1.1 with new reach, height and free-space rules; its numbers do not correspond to V3.2.1.

rows.title: Obstructed forward reach (with design constraints)
rows.summary: Where functional or design constraints require a deeper front obstruction, it must be no higher than 800 mm and no deeper than 510 mm (Set 2).
rows.changeNote: Clause 8.3 (stationary ICT) was rewritten in V4.1.1 with new reach, height and free-space rules; its numbers do not correspond to V3.2.1.

rows.title: Obstructed side reach (no design constraints)
rows.summary: Where stationary ICT has an integral obstruction to the side of the controls and nothing requires it to be deeper than 300 mm, the obstruction must be no higher than 800 mm and no deeper than 300 mm (Set 1).

rows.title: Assistive technology
rows.summary: Assistive technology itself must use the documented platform accessibility services.

rows.title: Object information
rows.summary: The role, states, boundary, name, and description of every user interface element must be programmatically determinable by assistive technology.

rows.title: Row, column, and headers
rows.summary: The row, column, and any headers of each data table cell must be programmatically determinable by assistive technology.

rows.title: Values
rows.summary: Current, minimum, and maximum values of a ranged element (such as a slider) must be programmatically determinable by assistive technology.

rows.title: Label relationships
rows.summary: Label relationships between elements (labels and labelled-by) must be exposed to assistive technology.

rows.title: Parent-child relationships
rows.summary: Parent-child relationships between elements must be programmatically determinable by assistive technology.

rows.title: Text
rows.summary: Text contents, text attributes, and the boundary of text on screen must be programmatically determinable by assistive technology.

rows.title: List of available actions
rows.summary: A list of the actions available on an element must be programmatically determinable by assistive technology.

rows.title: Execution of available actions
rows.summary: Where security permits, assistive technology must be able to programmatically execute those exposed actions.

rows.title: Tracking of focus and selection attributes
rows.summary: Information needed to track focus, the text insertion point, and selection attributes must be exposed to assistive technology.

previous.title: Tracking of focus and selection attributes

rows.title: Modification of focus and selection attributes
rows.summary: Where security permits, assistive technology must be able to programmatically move focus, the text insertion point, and selection.

previous.title: Modification of focus and selection attributes

rows.title: Change notification
rows.summary: Assistive technology must be notified of changes to the programmatically determinable attributes of elements.

rows.title: Modifications of states and properties
rows.summary: Where security permits, assistive technology must be able to modify states and properties of elements, where the user can modify them.

rows.title: Modifications of values and text
rows.summary: Where security permits, assistive technology must be able to modify values and text of elements, where the user can modify them.

rows.title: User control of accessibility features
rows.summary: Platform software must give users control over the platform accessibility features documented as intended for users.

rows.title: No disruption of accessibility features
rows.summary: Software must not disrupt documented platform accessibility features, except when the user asks it to.

rows.title: User preferences
rows.summary: Software that is not isolated from its platform must follow the user's platform accessibility preference settings, such as colour filters, contrast, text size, pointer size, and text cursor, unless not following a setting is essential to the software's function.

rows.summary: Information about a product that is made available digitally must itself conform to clause 9 (web), clause 10 (non-web document), or clause 11 (non-web software), depending on the format it is delivered in.
rows.changeNote: Was 12.1.2 (Accessible documentation) in V3.2.1.

rows.title: Accessible information about services
rows.summary: Information about a service, including support services, that is made available digitally must itself conform to clause 9 (web), clause 10 (non-web document), or clause 11 (non-web software), depending on the format it is delivered in.

rows.title: Accessibility and compatibility features
rows.summary: Product documentation must list and explain how to use the ICT's accessibility and compatibility features.
rows.changeNote: Was 12.1.1 (Accessibility and compatibility features) in V3.2.1.

rows.title: Electronic program guides
rows.summary: An electronic programme guide must provide information on whether subtitles, audio description, spoken subtitles, and sign language interpretation are available for the media it lists.

rows.title: Electronic program guide display
rows.summary: Where an electronic programme guide has information about the accessibility features of a media item, it must offer a mode in which users can find out whether subtitles, audio description, spoken subtitles, or sign language are available without activating the item.

rows.title: Use of the primary user destination address in relayed communications
rows.summary: Relay service invocation functions must use the destination addresses that primary users receive from their own communication systems, so the relay service does not require special numbers.

rows.title: Conveying of caller identifier in relayed communications for primary relay users
rows.summary: The caller identifier of a primary user of a relay service must be conveyed to the secondary user when the communication is established, unless the calling equipment is set to anonymous mode.

rows.title: Relay service invocation decision in outgoing communications
rows.summary: Primary users must be able to decide, by their own action at the moment they start an outgoing communication, whether a relay service is invoked.

rows.title: Relay service invocation decision in incoming communications
rows.summary: Primary users must be able to decide, by their own action at the moment they receive an incoming communication, whether a relay service is invoked.

rows.title: Relay service support requested by the primary user for emergency communications
rows.summary: On the primary user's request, the ICT must initiate and carry out an emergency communication and invoke the relay service in it.

rows.title: Relaying action in real-time bidirectional voice communication
rows.summary: A relay service must let primary users take part in speech communication with secondary users by converting modality (text, sign language, lip-speaking, clear speech) or providing communication support according to the type of relay service.

rows.title: Media handling in relay service communication
rows.summary: Relay service invocation functions must pass through any media that are not being converted but are enabled by the primary and secondary users' communication clients.

rows.title: Relay service support in ICT based conferences
rows.summary: A relay service must support the participation of primary users in conferences, with the extra modality conversion conveyed via the conference system or directly between the relay service and its user.

rows.title: Relay service support during emergency communications initiated by the PSAP
rows.summary: A relay service must accept invocations from emergency communication PSAPs, in a three-party fashion as specified in ETSI EN 303 919.
